verdict_reason: Solid coverage of the handshake context lifecycle; three minor gaps in resolve/sync behaviour-vs-implementation assertions and error-path propagation, no correctness or security concerns.

todos.issue: resolveHandshakeContext test 'prefers handshake fields from the POST payload' uses an empty session, so it does not guard against a regression where session is read before payload; a swapped-order bug would still pass.
todos.fix: Add a test that seeds the session with a different context, sends a payload with the new context, and asserts the returned/stored value is the payload's (not the session's).

todos.issue: syncHandshakeContext 'clears when GET query is absent' seeds an empty session, so the assertion that yar.clear was called does not prove a pre-existing handshake session would actually be wiped.
todos.fix: Seed the mock request with an existing handshake session, then call syncHandshakeContext with no query, and assert loadHandshakeContext(request) returns null (observable effect) rather than only that yar.clear was called.

todos.issue: resolveHandshakeContext has no test that a malformed POST payload (incomplete fields or unregistered journey type) propagates the Boom badRequest/notFound thrown by readHandshakePayload; a regression that swallowed the throw would go unnoticed.
todos.fix: Add two tests under 'resolveHandshakeContext' that pass a payload with only 'journey-type' (expect Boom.badRequest) and a payload with an unregistered journey type (expect Boom.notFound).
